claims.text: What the image looks like Pancreatic calcifications → chronic pancreatitis
W a typical Hx (heavy EToH use, recurr acute pancreatitis), pancreatic calcification on plain films may be sufficient; but it typically appears late and = visible in only ≈ 30%
claims.quote: In a patient with a typical history of heavy alcohol consumption and recurrent episodes of acute pancreatitis, detection of pancreatic calcification on plain radiographs of the abdomen may be sufficient. However, such calcifications typically occur late in the disease and then are visible in only approximately 30% of patients.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Calcifications to check: aorta (AAA), phleboliths, renal/ureteral stones, gallstones, pancreatic, appendicolith
claims.quote: Calcifications: aorta (AAA), phleboliths, renal/ureteral stones, gallstones (~10-15% radiopaque), pancreatic, appendicolith.

claims.text: CT detects calcifications, pseudocyst or dilated ducts but may be norm early; w.o a typical Hx, CT = typically recommended to exclude pancreatic CA
claims.quote: In patients without a typical history but with symptoms suggesting chronic pancreatitis, abdominal CT is typically recommended to exclude pancreatic cancer as the cause of pain. Abdominal CT can be used to detect calcifications and other pancreatic abnormalities (eg, pseudocyst or dilated ducts) but still may be normal early in the disease.

claims.text: EUS detects subtle parenchymal and ductal abnormalities; ↑sensitivity but limited specificity
claims.quote: Endoscopic ultrasound is less invasive and enables detection of subtle abnormalities in the pancreatic parenchyma and in the pancreatic duct. This imaging modality has a high sensitivity but limited specificity.

claims.text: Eti Persistent inflam causing permanent damage w fibrosis and ductal strictures, then declining exocrine and endo funct
claims.quote: Chronic pancreatitis is persistent inflammation of the pancreas that results in permanent structural damage with fibrosis and ductal strictures, followed by a decline in exocrine and endocrine function (pancreatic insufficiency).

claims.text: ≈ 50% from heavy EToH use (only a minority of heavy drinkers develop it); cigarette smoke = an indep, dose-dependent RF
claims.quote: Approximately 50% of cases of chronic pancreatitis result from heavy alcohol consumption, and chronic pancreatitis is more common among men than women (1). However, only a minority of people with sustained alcohol exposure ultimately develop chronic pancreatitis, suggesting that there are other cofactors required to trigger overt disease. Cigarette smoking is an independent, dose-dependent risk factor for developing chronic pancreatitis (2).

claims.text: Stone and duct obstruct theory: protein-rich plugs obstruct the ducts and may calcify into stones; chronic obstruct → fibrosis, ductal distortion, strictures and atrophy
claims.quote: The stone and duct obstruction theory proposes that disease is due to ductal obstruction caused by formation of protein-rich plugs as a result of protein–bicarbonate imbalance for unknown reasons. These plugs may calcify and eventually form stones within the pancreatic ducts. If obstruction is chronic, persistent inflammation leads to fibrosis, pancreatic ductal distortion, strictures, and atrophy.

claims.text: Sx Pain = present in most pts: USU postprandial, epigastric, and partly relieved by sitting up or leaning forward
claims.quote: Pain is often the dominant symptom in chronic pancreatitis and is present in most patients. Pain is usually postprandial, located in the epigastric area, and partially relieved by sitting up or leaning forward.

claims.text: When lipase and protease secretion falls below 10% of norm: steatorrhea (greasy stools); in severe cases undernutrition, wt loss and malabsorb of vitamins A, D, E and K
claims.quote: When lipase and protease secretions are reduced to < 10% of normal, the patient develops malabsorption characterized by steatorrhea, the passing of greasy stools, or even oil droplets that float in water and are difficult to flush. In severe cases, undernutrition, weight loss, and malabsorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K) may also occur.

claims.text: Tx and next step Her chart: stool elastase; EToH cessation; ERCP for ductal dz
claims.quote: Stool elastase; alcohol cessation; ERCP for ductal disease

claims.text: Encourage smoke cessation and EToH abstinence to slow progression; look for treatable comp such as duodenal or biliary obstruct
claims.quote: First, vigorous efforts and appropriate referrals to encourage smoking cessation and alcohol abstinence should be made for patients with chronic pancreatitis in an effort to slow the disease progression as early as possible. Second, treatable complications of chronic pancreatitis such as duodenal or biliary obstruction that can cause similar symptoms should be sought.
Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (replacement of deficient hormones to treat pancreatic insufficiency) is used to treat steatorrhea

claims.text: Endoscopic therapy decompresses a duct obstructed by stricture or stones and may relieve pain in carefully selected pts (eg, ERCP w sphincterotomy, stent or dilate for a papillary or dist duct stricture)
claims.quote: Endoscopic therapy is aimed at decompressing a pancreatic duct obstructed by stricture, stones, or both and may provide pain relief in carefully selected patients with appropriate ductal anatomy. If there is significant stricture at the papilla or distal pancreatic duct, endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with sphincterotomy, stent placement, or dilation may be effective
Surgical treatment is effective for pain relief.
